title: "Lecture notes"
subtitle: "Guided explanations, examples, questions, and in-class activities"
---

Lecture pages provide the course narrative. Related practice and submissions appear under [labs and activities](../activities/index.qmd) and [assignments](../assignments/index.qmd).

## Week 1

- [Is a database just a glorified spreadsheet?](week-01-database-or-spreadsheet.qmd) — Where tabular files work, where they break, and what keys, relationships, constraints, and transactions add.

## Week 2

- [Why describe data as relations?](week-02-from-tables-to-relations.qmd) — Relational vocabulary, keys, relationships, and why formal data descriptions help before we discuss query languages.
- [Activity 2 — Relations and keys](../activities/week-02-relations-and-keys.qmd) — Practice describing schemas, identifying keys, choosing primary keys, and locating foreign keys.
- [Relational algebra and query meaning](week-02-relational-algebra.qmd) — Selection, projection, Cartesian product, join, closure, and the idea that one query meaning can correspond to multiple execution strategies.
- [Assignment 1 — Implement relational operators](../assignments/assignment-01-relational-operators.qmd) — Implement and test selection, projection, and rename over a small in-memory relation.

## Week 3

- [Defining tables with PostgreSQL](week-03-defining-relations-with-sql.qmd) — Translate relational schemas into PostgreSQL types, constraints, table definitions, and controlled changes to stored tuples.
- [Asking precise questions with SQL](week-03-asking-questions-with-sql.qmd) — Use selection, projection, expressions, ordering, and nulls to retrieve the intended tuples and attributes.
- [Lab 2 — Ask it, write it, break it](../activities/week-03-query-reasoning-lab.qmd) — Translate questions into SQL, predict results, and construct boundary cases that distinguish correct queries from plausible mistakes.
